about: Forge Cellars brings together Rick Rainey, the New York winegrower who runs its vineyards, and Louis Barruol of Château de Saint Cosme in Gigondas, one of the southern Rhône’s most respected estates. Since their first vintage in 2011 on the east side of Seneca Lake, they have built a reputation for wines that show the character of individual vineyards, bottling their best sites separately alongside the blended “Classique” wines.

Caywood is one of Forge’s signature sites, on the southeast shore of Seneca Lake at about 970 feet, with older plantings from the 1970s lower down toward the water. It is best known for Forge’s Caywood Rieslings and Chardonnay. Cabernet Franc joined the Forge range in 2019, and like the rest of the wines it is hand-harvested and fermented spontaneously with native yeasts, with minimal intervention in the cellar.

Where the Willow bottling is bright and northern, a single-vineyard Cabernet Franc like this aims for more depth and an Old World profile: wild red and dark fruit, earth and wild herbs, with fine tannins and lake-driven freshness. Seneca Lake’s depth keeps the surrounding slopes milder in autumn and winter, which is what lets a late-ripening red like Cabernet Franc succeed this far north. Serve it with lamb, duck or mushroom dishes from the wood fire.
facts: Caywood Vineyard, southeast shore of Seneca Lake (about 970 ft)
